solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Guys in forest got wild flowers

indicators.note: the guys are placed in among the rearranged letters of the next two words
wild suggests the letters of forest and got run riot into a new order

parts.note: guys are men

explanation.surface: Some blokes wander into a wood and come across a patch of wild blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' looks like it describes the flowers, but it signals the anagram; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Forget-me-nots are small blue garden and woodland plants, an example of flowers.

clue.text: Cheats receiving criticism for such nonsense

indicators.note: receiving means the word for cheats takes the criticism into itself

parts.note: to fiddle is to cheat, so fiddles means cheats
stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in 'getting stick'

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses cheats who are being criticised as talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' meaning criticism, as in 'taking stick', is British slang; 'receiving' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation dismissing something as rubbish.

clue.text: Perch in river and ducks on street

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two O's

explanation.surface: A bird sits by the river while ducks paddle along a street.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, so 'ducks' gives two O's.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a place where birds settle to rest, a perch.

clue.text: Ruler exercises right during more rioting

indicators.note: during means the exercises and right come in the middle of the other letters
rioting tells us the letters of more are thrown into disorder

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A ruler asserts his rights while ever more unrest breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' makes EMOR, and 'during' splits it after its first two letters to take the exercises and right.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the sovereign of an empire, the highest kind of ruler.

clue.text: Airman out of place in yacht station

indicators.note: out of place says the letters of airman are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A pilot feels awkward among the sailing boats at a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour where yachts and pleasure boats are moored, a station for them.

clue.text: Queen almost raised in African republic

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters are read from the bottom up
almost means the last letter of the word for queen is dropped

parts.note: Regina is Latin for queen, used in official British titles

explanation.surface: A queen is nearly crowned or elevated in an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of REGINA to leave REGIN, which 'raised' turns upward into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked republic in West Africa.

clue.text: Large tavern in European capital

parts.note: tall can mean large in height
an inn is a tavern

explanation.surface: A big pub found in a city somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn is the capital city of Estonia.

clue.text: Stand-in monarch's grin — pretence, somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of grin and pretence are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A deputy king wears a fake smile.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'monarch' is a link meaning 'is'; the anagram signal follows the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince regent rules in place of a monarch unable to reign, as George IV did for George III.

clue.text: Become dejected when inferior diamonds returned

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of letters is read back the other way

parts.note: poor means inferior in quality
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: A card player loses heart when the diamonds given back are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: POOR plus D gives POORD, which 'returned' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag, and figuratively to flag or lose spirit.

clue.text: Typical long-standing customer

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means normal or typical
someone who frequently visits the same shop or pub

explanation.surface: A typical loyal customer who has been coming for years.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means both usual and, as a noun, a habitual patron.

clue.text: Subsequently learn to abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters of learn to are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Later on, someone will go overseas to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on and subsequently both mean at a following time.

clue.text: Rule, then abdicate, failing to produce son

indicators.note: failing to produce a son means the S drops out of the word

parts.note: to abdicate is to resign a throne
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A king rules, then gives up the throne for lack of a male heir.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a monarch's rule or period on the throne.

clue.text: Splendid salesman aboard bus heading west

indicators.note: in an across entry heading west means reading from right to left
aboard means the salesman goes inside the bus

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman rides a westbound bus and finds it excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' makes BREPUS, and 'heading west' reads it right to left in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent or magnificent, a close synonym of splendid.

clue.text: Coppers welcoming an act of contrition

indicators.note: welcoming means the coins take the next word into themselves

parts.note: coppers are copper coins, British pence

explanation.surface: Police officers allow someone to show remorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here means pennies: British 1p and 2p coins are called coppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken to show sorrow for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Bad smell in small English boozer

indicators.note: in says the bad smell is placed between the two abbreviations

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A stink lingers in a cramped English pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, but here it means a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge is informal for a person who drinks a lot, one who soaks it up.

clue.text: Offer in favour of model

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to model is to pose for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A proposal supporting some model or exemplar.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward a suggestion, to offer it for consideration.

clue.text: Outlaw group over it

parts.note: a band is a group of people

explanation.surface: A gang of outlaws hands the loot over.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, an outlaw.

clue.text: Fashionable fool, would you not agree?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: Someone asks for agreement that a trendy person is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is British slang contraction of 'isn't it', used as a tag inviting agreement.

clue.text: Time, approximately, for delivery of trunk

parts.note: or so means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: Someone asks roughly when a trunk will be delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests luggage being delivered, but it is the body's central part.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Messenger's job secured by porter

indicators.note: secured by means the job is held inside the drink

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A messenger's employment is obtained through a doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' looks like a doorman but is a dark beer. The 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle, from Greek for 'one sent out', is a messenger who spreads a teaching.

clue.text: Stressful past, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the past is one example of a grammatical ...

explanation.surface: A stressful time in someone's past.
explanation.definitionFit: Tense is both an adjective for nervy strain and a grammar term of which past is one.

clue.text: Similar type visually embarrassed

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
an embarrassed person visibly turns red in the face

explanation.surface: A like-minded sort of person who blushes noticeably.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred as an adjective means of like nature, related or alike.

clue.text: Small amount of exuberance, head being absent

indicators.note: head being absent means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: bounce means liveliness, exuberance

explanation.surface: Someone has only a little exuberance left with no leader present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head being absent' drops the B from BOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, so 'an ounce of' means a tiny amount.

clue.text: Having lost bottle, he blew unfairly

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters of bottle, he and blew have gone astray into a new order

explanation.surface: After losing his nerve, a man cheated at the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost bottle' reads as British slang for losing one's nerve; 'lost' is the anagram signal on BOTTLE HE BLEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the belt is an idiom from boxing, where low punches are illegal, so it means unfairly.
